mutants.expected_detection: SR1 instrumented iteration/comparison counting test will show that the number of comparisons executed varies with the position of the first mismatching byte: adversarial blocks with a mismatch at position 15 (checked first, going backward from the end) will terminate the scan almost immediately, while a mismatch near the start of the padding region (or fully valid padding) will require scanning through most/all of the 16 positions. This reproduces the classic Vaudenay padding-oracle timing signal and violates the required constant iteration count across mismatch-position/validity classes.

SR2 known-answer equivalence test will fail: for valid padding of length N, the reference expects *unpadded_len == 16-N, but this mutant writes 16-n+1 (off by one), producing wrong unpadded_len for every valid-padding vector across lengths 1..16, causing bitwise-equality assertions against the reference oracle to fail.

Static fail-on-presence scan of pad_check body detects a `break` statement inside the loop over block[] that is guarded by a condition depending on block-derived byte comparison (per_position_bad), executed before the final unconditional write of *valid/*unpadded_len; additionally SR1 behavioral timing/iteration-count test will show iteration counts that vary with the position of the first mismatch, since the loop now exits early once a mismatch is found instead of always completing all 16 iterations.

FR1 known-answer vectors for valid padding of every length 1-16 will fail: unpadded_len will be off by one (15-n instead of 16-n), producing a wrong plaintext length whenever padding is valid, causing bit-exact comparison against the reference oracle to fail.

SR2/FR2 known-answer vectors: a block whose last byte is exactly 16 (valid boundary) or in range 1..15 will be misclassified due to the flipped comparison bound, and more importantly blocks with last byte 0 (which should be invalid per FR2) will now pass the len_ok check as 'n <= 16' remains true while the lower bound check is inverted to n > 1, causing last byte 0 or 1 to be mishandled -- producing *valid/*unpadded_len outputs that mismatch the reference oracle for last-byte-boundary invalid cases.

SR2/FR3 known-answer test with an adversarial block where the last byte N is in 1..16 but a byte outside the padding region (position < 16-N) happens to differ from N while all actual padding bytes (positions 16-N..15) DO match N will incorrectly be reported invalid, and more importantly a block where a byte OUTSIDE the padding window mismatches N no longer changes the mismatch mask correctly because per_position_bad is now computed without gating on in_region, causing byte_matches alone (not in_region & !byte_matches) to decide mismatch; this flips valid/unpadded_len results relative to the reference oracle for many crafted blocks, violating FR3's exact-match requirement.

g++ compilation of inputs/cbc_unpad.cpp as a standalone C++11 translation unit fails because the mutant introduces a C++17-only construct (a constexpr if with a structured-binding-style declaration and a nested namespace using-declaration that requires C++17), violating FR4's requirement that the file compile standalone with g++ under C++11 or later with no external dependencies. The build step of the harness (invoked with -std=c++11) will report a compilation error, causing all downstream FR1-FR4/SR1-SR3 test executions to be unavailable and the submission to fail synthesis_pass_rate.
